To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
neuritogenesis induced by genipin in PC12h, but not in PC 12 cells, is due to the presence of neuronal NOS protein.
a natural irridoid compound, genpin, induces neuritogenesis mediated by nitric oxides in PC12h but not PC12 cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a novel neuritogenic compound, geniposide, which has been isolated from the fruit of Gardenia jasminoides.
the elucidation of the molecular mechanism underlying genipin-induced neuritogenesis in the NOS-expressive cells.
the role of NOS innately expressed in NOS-expressed cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
neuronal NOS has an indispensable role in neurite outgrowth, and the neuritogenic effect of genipin is due to its NO production in NOS-expressed cells.
the neuritogenic response of PC12h to genipin is dependent on the innately expressed neuronal nitric oxide synthase.
the neuronal NOS protein is innately expressed in NOS-expressed cells and has a functional role for neuritogenesis in these cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
genipin induces neuronal differentiation through the up-regulation of neuronal NOS expression, which is innately expressed in the PC12h cells.
the iridoid compound genipin induces neurite outgrowh in PC12h and N1E-115 cells by up-regulating neuronal NOS activity through inhibition of arginase.
the neuronal NOS protein expressed in PC12 cells is not functional in neurite outgrowth but can become functional in the presence of a suitable substrate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of NOS is a key factor in the induction of neurite outgrowth.
the neuronal nitric oxide synthase (nNOS) is a critical mediator in neuronal differentiation.
neuronal NOS is a potential therapeutic target for neuroprotection and regeneration in neurodegenerative diseases.
